newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's forint firms vs basket after Czech moves.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's forint firms vs basket after Czech moves.

text.p: The Hungarian forint firmed slightly against the central bank (NBH) basket on Tuesday, with foreign investor interest increasing after the Czech central bank allowed the crown to float, dealers said.
The forint ended at 181.80/85 to the dollar, unchanged from midday, but 20 pips below the NBH resistance level or bid, compared with some 25 pips in the morning.
"We saw foreign investors liquidating positions while there was trouble out there (in the Czech Republic)," said Istvan Gere of ING Bank. "Today we already saw the reverse movement."
Intense pressure on the crown in the past two weeks resulted in it being allowed to float on Monday evening.

The battle over the crown had only a slight impact on the forint, which is usually pinned to the NBH bid but has been trading by up to 50 pips below the resistance level recently, dealers said, adding that Hungary's economic fundamentals were strong.
They attributed the forint's weakening to foreign investor concerns over the region amid the crown crisis and to usual end-month buying of foreign trade-related firms.

They said the forint may remain some 20 pips weaker than the NBH bid in the near future but they added this differential was small, representing some 0.1 percentage points within the NBH's 4.5 percent wide floating intervention band.
The forint floats against a currency basket made up 30 percent of the dollar and 70 percent of the mark.
